NDSACESXI01​​​​​​​​​​​​

Primary DNS server 192.168.40.2
Alternate DNS server
Hostname NDSACESXI01

NDSACESXI02

Primary DNS server 192.168.40.2
Alternate DNS server

NDSACESXI03​​​​​​​​​​​​

LocaleContent.title: Custom DNS Suffixes
LocaleContent.content:
In this section you will put the domain that your unit uses. This setting combined with the Hostname will generate your FQDN ( Fully Qualified Domain Name ) ex.: NDSACESXI01.MCCES.USMC.MIL ​​​​​. For this lab use this Domain MCCES.USMC.MIL ​​​​​​​

LocaleContent.title: Saving and Applying
LocaleContent.content:
Once you complete filling out each section of this menu, you can press ESC. A pop-up will appear asking “Apply changes and reboot host?” you will select Y yes. The host has to fully reboot to make the modifications.  ​​​​​​​

This is also the most basic way to send commands to your server, you will plug in a VGA cable and a Keyboard. but for the purpose of this class we will only concern ourselves with setting up the Network Configuration​​​​​​​ of the server. Once that is completed we will manage everything from the GUI (Graphical User Interface) which is more user-friendly for beginners. The image below is what you see when you access the DCUI of your ESXi (Elastic Sky X Integrated)

LocaleContent.title: Setting up storage
LocaleContent.content: To finish setting up the storage for your server you will need to have 500gb of disk space on your datastore. Repeat the previous steps until you reach 500gb, which is required for LAB02.

LocaleContent.title: Setting up Storage
LocaleContent.content:
For setting up storage for your server, you can take two main routes. The first one and most rudimentary, is creating a VMFS (Virtual Machine File System) Datastore, this will allow you to pool/ connect all the different hard drives in a server to make one big virtual hard drive, but it is restrained to that specific host meaning if those hard disk drives are not physically attached to that server, you will not be able to add it to the VMFS Datastore. (ex.: 100gb HDD + 100gb HDD + 100gb HDD = 300gb virtual HDD).

What happens if you have multiple servers? Well you would need to create something called vSAN (Storage Area Network) this datastore allows you to connect multiple disk from different servers into one big virtual Hard Disk. (ex.: server1 300gb + server2 300gb + server3 570gb = 1.07Tb vSAN)

Capabilities VMFS vSAN

Allow user to connect individual HDDs together

(isolated to one ESXi host)

 YES YES

Allow user to connect individual HDDs over multiple ESXi host

(can connect up to 64 ESXi host together) 

 NO YES
Allow user to migrate powered on Virtual Machines NO YES

Fault tolerance

(one or more servers can be damaged without losing data)

 NO YES
Difficulty level to deploy easy hard

LocaleContent.title: Annex C LAB 01
LocaleContent.content:
Introduction: This course will go over how the Marine Corps creates virtual environment that hosts multiple servers into one device. This is called Virtualization. Using VMware, a type-1 hypervisor, to utilize one powerful computer that can be split into tiny sections that can run Active Directory (the service that you used to login to this laptop) or CUCM (Cisco Unified Call Manager, the server that host all of your IP Phones and phone numbers) and many others apps or appliances. In the past each of those servers or applications used to be ran by individual bare metal server, imagine a room with one laptop for each of the applications, you soon would notice that you have a very tall tower of laptops generating heat spending energy and occupying the room. Hence the Marine Corps transitioned to a virtual environment using VMware. This allowed marines to package all of the required capabilities into one green transit case permitting marines to take their servers out of the Data Centers and big building, straight into the field with them. 

​​​​​​​
